relations.subject: backup:archived-repository
relations.evidence: Archiving an repository moves the repository to read-only mode. This means that no more backup tasks will be run. The repository can still be restored and the data examined but not altered. This action is not reversible.

relations.subject: backup:imported-repository
relations.object: cannot use --remove-data on an imported repository
relations.evidence: This argument can only be used with archived repositories as imported ones could still be in use by another node.

notable_absence.finding: No RBAC role named anywhere, including for --remove --remove-data (an irreversible bulk-data-deletion action explicitly flagged 'once the data is deleted it cannot be recovered'). More striking: a flag-name inconsistency between the reference sections and the worked examples on the SAME page - OPTIONS documents the flag as '--plan <plan_name>' ('The plan to use as the base for the repository'), but every single EXAMPLES command that adds a repository uses '--profile' instead ('--add --id new-repository --profile _weekly --backup-archive /backup/service'), and the EXAMPLES prose even says 'is using a base profile _weekly. The base profile defines the schedules...'. The raw `usage:` line at the top of the page also spells it '--plan <plan_name>', confirming --plan is the real flag and every EXAMPLES invocation and its surrounding prose consistently uses the wrong flag name '--profile' instead. This is a strong, concrete instance of the round's flag-description-drift watch item, and specifically a terminology inconsistency (plan vs profile) for the exact concept - backup:plan - this round is centrally interested in.

cross_component_finding: Confirms backup:repository as 'the SAME construct whether written by cbbackupmgr CLI directly or the Backup Service's plan mechanism' - this page states outright that the --backup-archive location 'is equivalent to a cbbackupmgr archive' and warns cbbackupmgr must not be run directly against a service-managed archive, which is the clearest, most explicit statement anywhere in this batch of the shared-archive-format/separate-management-domain relationship between couchbase-cli backup-service and cbbackupmgr. Also relevant to the plan question: this repository sub-subcommand takes a plan/profile name as its schedule source ('The base profile defines the schedules of the tasks that the repository will run as well as what services it will backup'), so backup:plan is load-bearing at repository-creation time on this CLI surface too, not just in backup-service-plan.md.
